lines: We made it home without losing anyone. That is the ending I wanted.
The route was rough, but your directions held when the landmarks changed.
I am glad I followed you, though I would pack more food next time.
You kept checking that I was behind you. I noticed.
The journey looked shorter on the map than it felt under my boots.
I learned more from that road than I expected to.
We left together and returned together. A sound plan should manage that.
The weather turned, and you found shelter before I had to ask.
I was nervous when the village bell faded behind us.
Your pace made room for someone who spends more time standing at a lectern.
I marked the safe crossings while they were fresh in my memory.
There were moments I doubted the route, not the person leading it.
I would travel with you again after a quieter week at home.
The road widened my world and wore through one good pair of boots.
You warned me before the steep parts. Thank you for that.
I came back with notes, sore legs, and no serious regrets.
The best part of the trip was recognizing our own rooftops again.
I understand now why travelers remember meals and weather so clearly.
We handled the delays without turning on each other.
Next time I will bring the map and let you carry the heavier bag.
I made it back, but this injury belongs in any honest account of the trip.
The road cost more than either of us expected.
I need rest before I decide whether the journey was worth it.
You got me home after I could no longer keep pace.
This bandage is a strong argument for better planning.
I remember exactly where the trouble began and how far safety felt from there.
We should have turned back when the weather changed.
I kept walking because stopping there would have been worse.
Next time we carry medicine where we can reach it quickly.
I am grateful for the return and angry about the choices that made it difficult.
The wound will heal. I still want to understand how we let it happen.
You supported my weight for the last stretch. I will not forget that.
I mistook exhaustion for caution and paid for it.
The path home looked different once every step hurt.
I need fewer brave assurances and more warning before danger.
We reached shelter too late to avoid this, but early enough to save me.
I will record the route that injured me so nobody repeats it blindly.
There is blood on my notes, which makes the lesson hard to overlook.
I survived the trip. Give me time before asking for praise.
If we leave again, the return plan comes first.
Following you was an act of trust. You answered it with harm.
I kept watching the road because I never expected danger beside me.
Your betrayal changed every earlier kindness in my memory.
I wrote down what happened before shock could blur it.
Do not ask me to call that journey a misunderstanding.
You knew I depended on you to get home.
The worst wound came from learning whose hand caused it.
I followed your directions because I believed you meant to keep me safe.
No map warns a traveler that the guide may turn on them.
I reached the village without your help. Remember that.
You made every promise from that trip sound false afterward.
I will not travel with you again simply because you regret the result.
Trust does not return by the same road it left.
I remember the exact moment I understood what you were doing.
There were dangers all around us, and you chose to become another one.
Keep your distance while I decide what place you have in my life now.
The village deserves the true account, not the version that protects you.
I am home, but I do not feel safe around you.
You cannot repair this by pretending the journey ended normally.
I believed you once. That fact now belongs to the warning.
The boat carried us home, though my bag will smell of river for days.
I would have packed fewer books if you had mentioned the water.
The crossing was calm until the wind found us halfway over.
You kept the boat straight while I kept the supplies from sliding.
I have never been so pleased to step onto mud.
The shore vanished faster than I expected behind us.
We followed the stars when the banks became too dark to read.
One oar creaked the entire way, and I listened to every sound.
The boat sat lower after we took on the extra bundle.
I learned that ink, spray, and poor packing make terrible company.
You chose a sheltered landing when the current strengthened.
The river shortened the route and lengthened my list of worries.
I could not mark the turns quickly enough from the moving boat.
We passed under trees that made the water feel like a tunnel.
The current did more of the steering than either of us admitted.
I watched the clouds because there was nowhere nearby to shelter.
Next time I am wrapping every page in waxed cloth.
The trip was beautiful once my stomach settled.
You brought us alongside the dock without breaking anything important.
I would travel by boat again, but not without asking where we land.
